note_tweet.text:
OpenAI's engineers now let an AI agent take the 3 a.m. page.

Their "dots" are always-on agents that watch channels, run on-call incidents, open investigation threads, scan codebases, and draft PRs. One engineer handled a page from the ChatGPT app without getting up. They've helped merge 1,400+ PRs and delete 800,000 lines of code. How I'd give a small team its first always-on agent:

1. Start with one channel, not the whole company
2. Agent opens the thread, human closes the incident
3. It drafts the fix PR, a person merges it
4. Give it the runbook before you give it access
5. Read-only on prod until it earns more
6. Every page it handles gets a short write-up
7. Let it delete dead code, reviewed in small PRs
8. Measure pages you slept through, not tokens spent

The best agent job is the one nobody wants at 3 a.m.

#OpenAI #AIAgents #DevOps #AICoding #DevTools

note_tweet.text:
Silicon Valley's dirtiest open secret: enterprise AI has a retention problem. Companies spend millions deploying copilots, employees play with them for two weeks, hit a few hallucinations, and abandon the tab forever.

Elon says Grok Bot is doing the exact opposite - weekly usage per user is compounding, and he's calling it the fastest-growing product he's ever built.

The structural difference? @Grok doesn't sit there waiting for someone to type into an empty prompt box. xAI wired the full compute of the Colossus supercluster straight into the unfiltered, live 𝕏 firehose - and turned it into an autonomous background agent tracking competitors, supply chains, and market shifts 24/7.

Enterprise software never needed another polite chatbot. It needed an aggressive real-time intelligence desk.

The sterile copilots are living on borrowed time 🤖 https://t.co/JOtJo9qFzx
